topicName: Logic Controllers (If, Loop, Transaction, While, Switch)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Logic Controllers in Apache JMeter"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Logic Controllers in Apache JMeter dictate the order of execution of samplers and requests within your Test Plan. By default, JMeter runs samplers in a sequential top-to-bottom order. Logic Controllers allow you to introduce conditional branching, looping, transactions, and dynamic workflows to simulate realistic user behavior."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. If Controller"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The If Controller allows you to run its child elements conditionally, based on the evaluation of a JavaScript or __groovy expression. If the expression evaluates to true, the child elements are executed; otherwise, they are skipped."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configuration: Check "Interpret Condition as Variable Expression?" if you are simply checking a variable value to optimize performance."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Best Practice: Prefer Groovy syntax for evaluation, such as "${__groovy(vars.get("status")=="success")}"."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Loop Controller"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Loop Controller keeps its child elements running for a specified number of iterations. This is distinct from Thread Group loops, as it applies only to the specific samplers nested directly under the Loop Controller."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"Thread Group (Loops: 1)
  --> Loop Controller (Loop Count: 5)
      --> HTTP Request (Search Product)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the example above, the HTTP Request will execute exactly 5 times per thread execution."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. While Controller"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The While Controller runs its children until the condition returns "LAST" or evaluates to false. It is commonly used for polling mechanisms, such as waiting for a background process or file generation to complete."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Condition empty: Loops until a child sampler fails."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Condition string "LAST": Loops until the last child sampler fails."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Custom Condition: Loops while the condition evaluates to true, e.g., "${__groovy(!vars.get("isReady").toBoolean())}"."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Transaction Controller"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Transaction Controller measures the total time taken to execute all its nested child samplers. It aggregates the response times of multiple requests into a single virtual transaction, which is vital for end-to-end business scenario metrics (e.g., "Checkout Process")."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Generate parent sample: Check this box to group all child samplers under a single aggregated transaction result in listeners."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Include duration of timer: Check to include pauses (timers) inside the overall transaction time."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Switch Controller"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Switch Controller acts like a switch-case statement. It evaluates a given value or index and executes only the matching child element. If the value does not match any element name, it falls back to executing the element at index 0 (or the default element)."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"Switch Value: ${userType}
  --> Child 1: admin_flow
  --> Child 2: guest_flow
  --> Child 3: vendor_flow"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"If the variable ${userType} evaluates to "guest_flow", JMeter will exclusively run the child sampler/controller named "guest_flow" and skip the others."},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Combining Logic Controllers allows you to build dynamic, resilient, and enterprise-grade performance test scripts in JMeter. Always validate your control flow using the View Results Tree listener in non-load test mode before executing massive concurrent tests."}]
